page: Amazon Web Services c7g.large is an arm64 compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform runs on an AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processor operating at 2.6 GHz, providing 2 physical cores configured as 2 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per core. The processor cache hierarchy consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware cryptographic support for AES. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Networking operates with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and the configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate steady single-thread performance alongside bounded multi-core throughput due to the dual-core hardware envelope. Single-core measurements include a Geekbench single-core score of 1437.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1532.38, and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 24.18 GB/sec. Uncached large block read memory bandwidth reached 52.81 GB/sec. Multi-core and aggregate tests align with low-capacity scaling: Geekbench multi-core reached 2580.0, stress-ng multi-core achieved 3043.08, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression measured 16.2 GB/sec. In application-oriented tests, the machine produced 3.41 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.54 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The c7g.large offers high execution predictability by assigning unshared physical cores rather than simultaneous multi-threading threads. The primary architectural tradeoff is the small memory capacity and total absence of local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage for stateful data. The instance provides a cost-efficient footprint for ARM-compatible utility tasks, distributed microservices, CI/CD build agents, and lightweight web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Neoverse-V1 processor on the Nitro hypervisor. Featuring 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs clocked at 2.6 GHz, the system provides 4.0 GB of memory at a ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The CPU includes 32 MB of L3 cache and hardware-supported AES cryptography. The platform contains no bundled local storage, lacks GPU accelerators, and maintains a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations reflect solid single-core throughput, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1437.0 and large-block read memory bandwidth of 52.81 GB/sec, while overall multi-threaded capacity remains bounded by the two-core design. Offering qualitative cost efficiency through dedicated ARM silicon, the c7g.large is suitable for lightweight web serving, microservices, and continuous integration agents.
